contact.title: Contact UsageNow support
contact.body: Let us know your device model, iOS version, app version, which service the account belongs to, what you tapped, and roughly when it happened. Never send a password, sign-in code, access token, or screenshot that shows one.

footer: Official support and privacy information for UsageNow: AI Usage Tracker.

home.title: See what is left of every AI plan at a glance
home.summary: UsageNow shows how much of each AI subscription you have used and exactly when it resets, in the app, on Home Screen widgets and on Apple Watch. It talks directly to each service from your device; there is no UsageNow server.

sections.title: Direct from your device
sections.body: You add an account through that service's own sign-in page. When the app or its widget refreshes, your iPhone or iPad asks the service's API for your usage directly over HTTPS. Nothing passes through a UsageNow server, because there is none.

sections.title: Sign-ins stay in the Keychain
sections.body: Sign-in tokens are stored only in this device's Keychain with AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly protection. They are shared only with the UsageNow Home Screen Widget so it can refresh by itself, and they are not synced to iCloud or sent to Apple Watch.

sections.title: Widgets and Apple Watch
sections.body: The Widget and Apple Watch show the latest usage percentages and reset times. The paired Apple Watch receives only that snapshot, never a sign-in token.

sections.title: 24-hour free trial, then one purchase
sections.body: Every feature is free for 24 hours after you tap Start 24-Hour Free Trial. UsageNow Pro is a one-time purchase through StoreKit with the price shown in your local currency. There is no subscription and no advertising.

support.title: UsageNow Support
support.summary: Help with adding accounts, refreshing usage, widgets, Apple Watch, the free trial and UsageNow Pro.

sections.title: Add an account or try sample data
sections.body: Tap a service card or the plus button and sign in on that service's own page in Apple's secure web sheet; GitHub shows a short device code to enter. You can add several accounts per service. To explore first, tap Preview with sample data on the first screen.

sections.title: An account says Sign in again
sections.body: The service ended the session, for example after a password change, a sign-out on its website, or a long time without use. Tap Sign in again on that card. UsageNow never sees or stores your password.

sections.title: Widget numbers look old
sections.body: The Home Screen Widget refreshes itself approximately every 20 minutes when iOS allows it, and the refresh button on the Widget asks for new numbers right away. Low Power Mode or a poor connection can delay updates. Opening the app always refreshes every account.

sections.title: Offline or busy service
sections.body: If there is no connection or a service answers 429 Too Many Requests, UsageNow keeps the last numbers with their time and tries again later. Repeated taps do not get around a service's limits.

sections.title: Sort accounts and change language
sections.body: With two or more accounts, use the sort button to order them by service, soonest reset, most used, least used, name or your own order. Settings lets you pick any of 50 languages or follow the system language; the Widget and Apple Watch follow.

sections.title: Sign out and remove data
sections.body: Use the account menu and choose Sign out to delete that account's tokens from the Keychain and its numbers from the app, Widget and Apple Watch. To remove everything, sign out of each account and then delete the app. You can also revoke access in each service's own account settings.

sections.title: Free trial, UsageNow Pro and Restore
sections.body: The 24-hour free trial starts only when you tap it and runs once per Apple Account. After it ends, the app and widgets stay locked until you buy UsageNow Pro, a one-time StoreKit purchase that is not a subscription. Use Settings, Restore Purchases on any device signed in to the same Apple Account.

sections.title: What to include when you write
sections.body: Send your device model, iOS version, app version, the service name, what you tapped and the approximate time. Do not send a password, sign-in code, token or full sign-in URL. The developer cannot see your accounts and cannot recover them.

sections.title: Independent app
sections.body: UsageNow is an independent app. Claude and Anthropic, ChatGPT, Codex and OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, GitHub and Microsoft, and Gemini and Google are named only to show which accounts the app can read; UsageNow is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by them.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: UsageNow has no server, no account of its own, no advertising and no analytics. This policy explains exactly where your sign-ins and usage numbers go.

sections.title: Sign-in tokens
sections.body: Tokens from each service are stored only in this device's Keychain with AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly protection and are not synchronizable. Only the UsageNow app and its own Home Screen Widget can read them. They are never written to iCloud, sent to Apple Watch, or sent to the developer.

sections.title: Requests to each service
sections.body: To sign in and to refresh usage, your device contacts that service's own sign-in page and API directly over HTTPS. The service receives the request under its own privacy policy. UsageNow does not use a proxy, VPN, tunnel or developer server; during sign-in the app briefly listens on a local address on this device only to receive the sign-in reply.

sections.title: What the developer receives
sections.body: Nothing automatically. The developer does not receive your tokens, account email, plan, usage numbers or reset times, and there is no UsageNow account or database.

sections.title: Stored on your device
sections.body: The app keeps the latest usage snapshot (account label, plan name, usage percentages, reset times and the time of the last refresh), your sort order, language choice, trial end time and a short local log of Widget button taps for troubleshooting. This stays on the device.

sections.title: Widget and Apple Watch
sections.body: The app and Widget share the snapshot through an App Group on this device. WatchConnectivity sends the same snapshot to your paired Apple Watch so its app and complications can show it; tokens are not included.

sections.title: Purchases
sections.body: StoreKit contacts Apple to show the local price, start the free trial, buy UsageNow Pro and Restore Purchases. Apple processes payment; the developer does not receive your payment details.

sections.title: No ads, analytics or tracking
sections.body: UsageNow contains no advertising, no third-party analytics, no crash-reporting service and no tracking across apps or websites. It does not sell data, does not build profiles and does not ask for your password.

sections.title: Deleting your data
sections.body: Signing out of an account deletes its tokens from the Keychain and removes its numbers from the app, Widget and Apple Watch. Signing out of every account and deleting the app removes the rest. You can also revoke UsageNow's access in each service's account settings.

sections.title: Support email and this website
sections.body: If you email support, the developer receives only the address and message you choose to send and uses them only to reply. This website sets no cookies and loads no advertising, analytics or tracking scripts; GitHub Pages hosts it and may process standard connection data under its own terms.

sections.title: Independent app
sections.body: UsageNow is an independent app. Claude and Anthropic, ChatGPT, Codex and OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, GitHub and Microsoft, and Gemini and Google are named only to show which accounts the app can read; UsageNow is not affiliated with, sponsored or endorsed by them.

sections.title: Changes and questions
sections.body: If this policy changes, the new version is posted here with a new date. UsageNow is not directed to children. Questions about privacy can be sent to the support email below.
